## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mahālomahaṁsacariya* ("The Hair-raising Conduct"), cataloged as Cp 35 (or Cp III.15), is a narrative poem preserved in the *Cariyāpiṭaka* of the Khuddaka Nikāya [Norman 1983]. The text serves as the canonical illustration of the Bodhisatta's fulfillment of the perfection of equanimity (*upekkhā-pāramī*) [War Yar Mein Da 2015]. In the verse account, the Bodhisatta lies down in a cemetery upon the bones of skeletons, remaining entirely detached and imperturbable with equal-minded forbearance whether cowherds come to revile and mock him or others honor and praise him [Bareau; War Yar Mein Da 2015]. Kenneth Roy Norman notes that this text is to be compared with the *Mahāsīhanādasutta* of the Majjhima Nikāya [Norman 1983].
